title: Death toll from Russian missile strike on Pryluky rises to nine: bodies of three children recovered from under rubble – video

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Death toll from Russian missile strike on Pryluky rises to nine: bodies of three children recovered from under rubble – video

The death toll from a Russian missile strike on Pryluky has risen to nine, including three children, and 38 people have been injured.

Actual Article Body:

The death toll from a Russian missile strike on Pryluky in Chernihiv Oblast has risen to nine, and 38 people have been injured. Rescue workers are still clearing the rubble.

Source: Chernihiv Oblast Police; Ukrainian public broadcaster Suspilne

Quote: "As of 11:30, the death toll has risen to nine. Sadly, the bodies of three children have been recovered from under the rubble of the apartment building.

Thirty-eight people have been injured, including seven children."

Details: Search and rescue operations are currently underway to find people trapped under the rubble.

Nina Lutsenko, spokesperson for the State Emergency Service in Chernihiv Oblast, said three people, including a child, had been rescued.

Five children aged three, five, eight and nine, as well as a police officer, are among those injured.

Actual Article Body:
Latvia’s Foreign Ministry has begun the process of declaring “another Russian citizen” persona non grata, Foreign Ministry head Baiba Braže said. She said the decision followed consultations with the Internal Affairs Minister and the prime minister and was based on information “from the competent authorities.”

Delfi reported that the case concerns Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin, who has lived in Latvia since 2014. Ragozin worked as a correspondent and producer for BBC Russia and as an editor of the magazine Russian Newsweek, and has more recently worked with Al Jazeera, Lonely Planet, Jacobin, and The American Conservative.
